findings.title: Cancellation can win after the final pre-dispatch check yet the configuration adapter is still invoked
Batch cleanup did not recheck an external writer after taking the HOME lease
Cancellation racing a pre-spawn adapter failure can revoke the captured admission certificate
Credential or dependency rotation during failure cannot redirect revocation from the captured scope
Preflight rejection without a captured verification reference preserves a newer certificate
Concurrent proposal completion returns a coherent state and payload snapshot
A native transcript change before the batch lease is detected and aborts all cleanup side effects
A physical native process can start but a PROCESS-journal failure misclassifies it as unstarted and lets cancellation preserve its certificate

limitations: I independently reconstructed the frozen source manifest: all 203 entries yield candidate SHA-256 `9f7b8206ee78d418ef4b0393b3f8c2797a313f0d96808b67e46d1dbe73a2a87c`, matching the supplied identity and declared tree `e776c10fb1a207340ff9ba460f7085a9488cf03a`. All 284 sealed r14-manifest entries matched their declared size and SHA-256; the contract hash also matched `5cb10d9a31d8c603db4a07151dfdf39fff32fcda3893e1061cfe3d03d931c352`.

The former R3 exception-path defect is fixed. `ModelAdmission._publish()` now reads cancellation and writes the certificate in one immediate transaction (`tools/studio/model_admission.py:74-89`), while the configuration exception path supplies `unless_cancelled` for an actually nonstarted process (`tools/studio/configuration_assistant.py:174-179`). My independent scratch test confirmed: cancellation committed first vetoes revocation; failure committed first remains revoked; and a newer full record with the same scope/key is protected by the exact-record CAS. Six focused shipped dispatch/certificate tests and five focused dependency/cleanup tests also passed locally.

A distinct remaining P1 boundary is reproducible. In a scratch-only test, I used the candidate's actual `orchestration.process._execute()` with a harmless local `sleep` child, then injected an `OSError` at `ConfigurationJournal.finish()` immediately after `Popen` but before its `PROCESS:RUNNING` read can set `journal.process_started` (`tools/orchestration/process.py:108-114`; `tools/studio/configuration_assistant.py:73-75`). The process had physically started and was safely killed by `_execute`'s exception cleanup; cancellation then committed before the assistant exception handler. The operation correctly ended `CANCELLED`, but because `process_started` remained false, the handler passed `unless_cancelled=key` and preserved the prior VERIFIED certificate. The durable journal retained `PROCESS:INTENT` and `CONFIGURATION_DISPATCH:CANCELLED`. This contradicts the intended started/nonstarted distinction: a process that has actually started must retain failure revocation even if journal publication fails.

The current shipped synthetic test only covers the intended started branch by manually assigning `args[-2].process_started=True` (`tests/test_session_configuration.py:377-382`). It does not establish that physical process creation and the `process_started` flag remain atomic when the intervening PROCESS journal update fails. The repair must carry an irrevocable started indication across that error boundary or otherwise conservatively revoke once `Popen` succeeds; it must retain the cancellation transaction and captured-record CAS protections.

The model-refresh and legacy initial-save corrections appear sound by source inspection and sealed current evidence. `ModelSelector` retains a stable refresh button, disabled state, `aria-busy`, and separate live status (`tools/studio/workbench_ui/ModelSelector.jsx:39-40`). `saveDraft` uses request ordering only for initial identity ownership while retaining revision CAS (`tools/studio/static/usable.js:130-143`). I inspected the preserved r12/r13 red evidence and the current r14 green records. A fresh local Chromium replay could not be made because this reviewer environment lacks both the recorded Chromium executable and Node/Playwright runtime; that is an environment limitation, not a product test failure.

I inspected rather than replayed the sealed broad evidence: 725 Python tests, 6 ordinary host tests, 56 JS editor/projection tests, 193 ordinary HTTP/Chromium checks, baseline, syntax, rebuild, privacy, catalog registration, the real configuration-to-apply-to-Codex/Claude workflow journey, and same-UUID native Codex/Claude terminal question-and-answer records. The separately executed normal-host 21-test supplement is external-runner evidence, not local reviewer execution. Its nested-host capabilities are not claimed here.

Real records support the required native configuration generation/application and same-UUID terminal claims, but physical backend identity and effective effort remain unknown. Model registration remains distinct from execution admission; proposal application remains draft-only; future Agent-mode workspace writes still require separate runtime confirmation.

No model call, authentication read, source/authority/Git/Stable write, external publication, merge, or promotion was performed in this review. The old Task03 limited accepts and old Gate BLOCKED records remain historical only. This report makes no formal technical acceptance or personal user-experience acceptance.
